description: a frustum of radius 0.5 at z = 0 and 0.27 at z = 1.25 about z, less a stub of radius 0.106 from (−0.025, 0.035, 0.456) inside it, 3 long along (0.183, −0.26, 0.948), which leaves through the cone wall — then the stub fused back onto what the cut left: `fuse(a − b, b)`, which is `a ∪ b`. The cut is right, and so is `fuse(a, b)` itself; the restoring fuse refuses the pair as `Unsupported`, the NURBS curve against the NURBS curve. The cone and the stub's wall meet in a traced section (ADR-0018) whose fitted spline depends on the region the boolean traces it in — the operands' box overlap grown by its diagonal, one per boolean so every face pair of one boolean gets the same curve bit for bit — and the region of `a − b` against `b` is not that of `a` against `b`: the section is fitted over other knots, and deciding that the cut's section edge lies along the fuse's own section is `curves_coincide` on two NURBS curves that are not the same spline, the pair only a marcher could decide. Rounding the direction to two digits or the radius to 0.1 makes the two fits the same spline again and the pair passes. Found by the quadric identities at a random pose in 256 (plans/c3-conic-hits step 8); the two cylinders' sections never see it, their loops not depending on the region. A backlog line: a traced section the same spline for the same two surfaces whatever the region, or two fits of one section decided coincident
